newsitem.title: UK: UK physical grains firm in active nervous trading.
newsitem.headline: UK physical grains firm in active nervous trading.

text.p: UK physical grain prices jumped by as much as 2.75 stg a tonne in active nervous trading on Thursday as shorts tried to get cover in anticipation of export business, traders said. "There are reports of some large slugs of wheat being done in the U.S. for export and people feel some houses in the States may seek cover in Europe because our wheat is cheaper," said one.
The bullish trend was further fuelled by bids for European Union (EU) rebates at Thursday weekly grain tender for more than a million tonnes of wheat.
At the tender the EU granted 477,700 tonnes of free-market soft wheat at 17.47 Ecus rebate and 76,550 tonnes of free-market barley at 30.50 Ecus.
Traders said the result would not send the market flying upwards but was friendly
"The result is friendly to indifferent, but what is interesting is the wheat rebate which seems fairly aggressive," said one trader.
At a normally quiet time of year for ex-farmer business any increase in demand tends to force both physical and futures prices higher.
In active fob market feed wheat was trading around 2.50 to 2.75 stg above Wednesday's levels with Jan/Mar fetching 100.50, 101 and 101.50 stg a tonne and March 102 stg a tonne.
Apr/Jun feed wheat traded at 102.50 and 102.75 and May 103 stg a tonne all for 2,400 tonnes loads in coasters ex-east coast ports.
Higher futures for a change did not bring the delivered business to a halt with traders report buying interest from all sides of the market.
Traded levels were around two stg above Wednesday's with feed wheat in East Anglia fetching up to 96 stg for Dec, 99 stg for Jan and 101 stg for Feb.
In Liverpool 100 stg was paid for Jan and 105.50 stg for Apr/Jun.
Jan/Mar in the Avon range traded up to 100 stg with the same prices paid in Tilbury.
Feed barley in East Anglia and the Avon range traded up to 100 stg for Jan/Mar.
No milling wheat business was reported.
